An area of low pressure located several hundred miles northeast  of Bermuda is moving north-northeastward at 15 to 20 mph.  The  associated shower activity remains disorganized and the circulation  is broad and elongated.  This system could still become a  short-lived tropical depression or storm tonight before encountering  increasingly hostile conditions by early Wednesday, likely ending  its chances for development. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

Showers and thunderstorms associated with an area of low pressure  centered a few hundred miles south-southeast of the Cabo Verde  Islands have changed little in organization over the past several  hours.  However, environmental conditions appear conducive for  gradual development, and this system is likely to become a tropical  depression during the next day or two while it moves westward to  west-northwestward across the eastern and central tropical Atlantic.  Environmental conditions could become less conducive for development  by the weekend. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

A tropical wave located well to the south of southern Mexico is  producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms. This system  has become become better organized since yesterday, and  environmental conditions appear favorable for further development.  A tropical depression is expected to form in a few days while it  moves generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well offshore  of Mexico. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

An area of low pressure could form well offshore of Central America  late this week or this weekend. Environmental conditions should support some gradual development of this system, and a tropical  depression could form late this weekend or early next week while it  moves westward to west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph well offshore  of southern Mexico. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the  Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and  thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the  trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions  appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical  depression is likely to form during the latter part of the week or  early this weekend while the system drifts northeastward, then  turns to the west-northwest. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian  Islands late this week.  Some gradual development is possible by  the weekend into early next week while the system moves slowly to  the west or west-northwest, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian  Islands. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.
